scene.note: The callout's values sit at the top of route_in.py, and your if blocks turn them into a plan the hill party can follow.

steps.note: The river gauge gives a level, and the ford has a limit.
Under Task 1 one question about the river picks one of the two routes.
Whatever the river does, route always ends up holding one of the two words.
The wind on the tops is one number.
Under Task 2 the branches are asked from the top, and only the first that is True runs.
The hill party hears one of three warnings.
Two things matter to the helicopter: daylight and the wind.
Under Task 3 one if asks both questions at once.
Exactly one line prints: the helicopter comes, or the team carries.
The casualty's name may be known, missed on the radio, or not asked yet.
Under Task 4 the if asks whether there is a name at all.
The party hears the name, or hears plainly that nobody knows it.
